issue.title: fix(timepicker): avoid unnecessary CSS class mutation in the DOM
perf(timepicker): replaced ngClass method calls with class fields
issue.body:
Binding to a method makes Angular call it every time a change detection happens. Depending on complexity of your app it could be quite often. Using string field is a lot cheaper without sacrificing on functionality.

issue.title: ngClass from component method restores original classes
issue.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Description I'm using Bootstrap tabs and ngClass to append additional classes. I found that when using a component method for ngClass that it seems the original classes are getting restored when a component within the tab container changes. This does not happen when using an object directly within ngClass or by using [class.] syntax. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-bypyy7 Notice that the 'active' class gets restored in the first example in the project, but not the others. ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:**

issue.title: Unnecessary class updates in DropDowns

repository.name: kendo-angular
repository.description: Issue tracker - Kendo UI for Angular

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
Some of the element classes are updated on each change detection cycle.

Seems to be caused by https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/25518
Reported in ticket 1406079.

**To Reproduce**
1. Navigate to https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-bx88tm in Chrome
1. Open any of the drop-downs
1. Inspect the drop-down list
1. Notice how the `k-list-scroller` class is changed on each change detection cycle

**Expected behavior**
The class should not be updated.

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/247917/56558112-38986a00-65a6-11e9-92c9-3a72df4882e2.png)

**Browser**
 - OSX 10.14
 - Chrome 73

rename.from: ngCLass causes unnecessary CSS class mutation in some cases
rename.to: ngClass causes unnecessary CSS class mutation even if computed classes are unchanged

body:
This issue has non-negligible performance impact on the real-life websites. Taking the https://angular.io/resources as the example, the rendering of this page takes ~300ms on my machine:

![Screen Shot 2022-12-01 at 16 10 18](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/973550/205108385-8735bd62-39fa-4d6c-91a1-7edeed13a78b.png)

By removing calls to `ngClass` calls that suffer from the problem described here (see experiment in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/48312) we are seeing 20x spped improvement (the rendering time goes down to ~16ms):
![Screen Shot 2022-12-01 at 16 10 35](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/973550/205108836-f7cebe8a-d817-4678-8ab9-a22fdd770a7d.png)

Given the real-life impact observed we should bump up priority of this issue. The fix itself should be 2-fold:
* short term: fix problematic pattern in AIO
* improve ngClass implementation so it doesn't suffer from the performance cliff in this particular usage scenario (that can be pretty common).

issue.body:
NgClass has non-negligable performance cost, especially if a
different object is provided as NgClass input (which was the case
for the NavItemComponent). The perfornace problem was noticed
in the scope of the INP score investigations while profiling the
https://angular.io/resources page. On this particular page replacing
NgClass usage with alternatives results in 20x (!) runtime perf
improvement. Such big improvement is possible since we avoid unneeded
CSS classes removal / adding in the DOM.

Part of https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/25518

Before:
![Screen Shot 2022-12-01 at 16 10 18](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/973550/205108385-8735bd62-39fa-4d6c-91a1-7edeed13a78b.png)

By removing calls to `ngClass` calls that suffer from the problem described here (see experiment in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/48312) we are seeing 20x spped improvement (the rendering time goes down to ~16ms):
![Screen Shot 2022-12-01 at 16 10 35](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/973550/205108836-f7cebe8a-d817-4678-8ab9-a22fdd770a7d.png)
